info.description:
Overview

The public API is a REST API allowing to interact with the Cockpit ITSM portal from other applications. Note that only a certain subset of functionality is exposed in this API.

How to connect

The API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication. To connect, you need two things:

  • Configure an OAuth 2.0 API access (scope: public-api) via the administration menu first. If no API access for the scope "public-api" is configured, the public API cannot be accessed.
  • Create an API user in the operator management section of the Administration menu.
Please check out the relevant FAQs for more information on configuring the public API.

For information on how to obtain an access token for the API, go to the /oauth2/token endpoint in the "Core - Authentication" section. The documentation allows to create requests using cURL, JavaScript etc.

Core concepts

API objects

A subset of application objects (API objects) can be managed via the API. Please refer to this API documentation on how to access and modify these objects. The object structure is described in the "models" section.

Object references

To reference an object from an API object, object references are used. An object reference contains the unique ID of the references object along with a textual representation of the object such as its name, description or reference. When sending object references to the API, only the ID is evaluated. The reference is ignored and can be omitted.

Example (JSON output): 

{
    "id": 12,
    "reference": "Object name"
}

Example (JSON input): 

{
    "id": 12
}

Object repository

Certain objects (non-API objects) are not managed via the API but are referenced from API objects. To be able to use these objects, they are listed in the object repository. This repository does not offer full search functionality - its only purpose is to create a mapping between object names, descriptions and references and their respective object IDs.

If an object in the repository is linked to a specific organization, this information is included in the repository. Aside from this, no other information is included in the repository data.

Example: Equipment types cannot be modified through the API but you may want to specify an equipment type when creating or modifying equipment data. To do so, you can find the ID of the equipment type you want to use in the object repository.

To make mapping of repository objects to objets in an external application easier, the repository objects can be exported to an Excel file (/api/repository/objects.xlsx).

Data formats

Input format

Objects can be sent to the API as either JSON or XML in UTF-8 charset. The output format is determined by the "contentType" header.

  • To input data in JSON format, use the content type "application/json".
  • To input data in XML format, use the content type "application/xml".

Output format

API output can be formatted as either JSON or XML. The output format is determined by the "Accept" HTTP header (application/json or application/xml). If no content type is specified, the data is returned in JSON format.

Example: To request a list of organizations in XML format you can use the URI /api/organization/list.xml. The same data in JSON format can be requested through /api/organization/list.json or /api/organization/list.

Date format

The API emits and accepts timestamps in ISO format with timezone information (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

Example: 2019-12-31T23:59:59.000Z
